title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text: The 2017 paper “Attention Is All You Need” by Vaswani et al. introduced the Transformer architecture, revolutionizing NLP.

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text: The 2017 paper “Attention Is All You Need” by Vaswani et al. introduced the Transformer architecture, revolutionizing NLP.

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text:
Key Contributions

Self-Attention Mechanism: Allows the model to weigh the importance of different words
Positional Encoding: Captures sequence order without recurrence
Multi-Head Attention: Enables learning different representation subspaces

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text:
Architecture
The Transformer consists of:

Encoder: Processes the input sequence
Decoder: Generates the output sequence
Attention Layers: Connect encoder and decoder

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text:
Mathematical Foundation
The attention mechanism is defined as:
\[
\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^T}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right)V
\]

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text:
Impact
This architecture became the foundation for: - BERT - GPT series - T5 - And many more modern language models

title: Attention Is All You Need - Paper Summary
text:
References
Vaswani et al. (2017). “Attention Is All You Need”. NeurIPS.

Introduction

title: Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
text:
Definition
For a function \(f(x)\) that is infinitely differentiable at point \(a\), the Taylor series is:
\[
f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!}(x-a)^n
\]
When \(a = 0\), this is called the Maclaurin series.

title: Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
text:
Common Examples

Exponential Function
\[
e^x = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^n}{n!} = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^3}{3!} + \cdots
\]


Sine Function
\[
\sin(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!} = x - \frac{x^3}{3!} + \frac{x^5}{5!} - \cdots
\]


Cosine Function
\[
\cos(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2!} + \frac{x^4}{4!} - \cdots
\]

title: Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
text:
Applications
Taylor series are used in:

Numerical approximations - Computing values of transcendental functions
Physics - Linearizing equations near equilibrium points

title: Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
text:
The Problem
Given \(n\) random points uniformly distributed on the circumference of a circle, what is the probability that their convex hull (the polygon formed by connecting them) contains the center?

title: Trapping the Center: A Journey into Geometric Probability
text:
Solution
The key insight: the center is contained if and only if no two consecutive points are more than 180° apart.
For \(n\) points, the probability is:
\[
P(n) = \frac{n-1}{2^{n-1}}
\]
